sections.h2: Which written notices can a landlord use in North Carolina?
sections.html:
Three tools exist. A notice to quit ends a periodic tenancy. A demand for past-due rent starts a ten-day clock. A lease breach or holdover supports a court complaint without any set number of days beyond what the lease says.

The rules sit in Chapter 42 of the General Statutes: 42-14 covers ending a tenancy, 42-3 covers rent demands, and 42-26 lists the grounds a court will hear.

An owner who plans to sell a rented house should pick the right tool first, because the choice sets the earliest date the house can be handed over empty.

sections.h2: How many days does each kind of tenancy get?
sections.html:
The length of the notice tracks the length of the rental period. Weekly tenants get the least time and annual tenants the most.

Type of tenancyNotice to quit under G.S. 42-14
Year to yearAt least one month before the current year ends
Month to monthSeven days
Week to weekTwo days
Space rental for a manufactured homeAt least 60 days before the current rental period ends

Source: G.S. 42-14, North Carolina General Assembly. A written lease with a fixed end date follows other logic: a tenant who stays past the term is a holdover, which is one of the grounds in G.S. 42-26. Read the lease for added notice terms before counting days.

sections.h2: What happens when rent goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The landlord demands every dollar of past-due rent. If the tenant lets ten days pass without paying, the lease term is forfeited and the landlord may re-enter through the courts. G.S. 42-3 speaks to leases that fix a date for rent.

Late fees run on a separate track under G.S. 42-46. Rent must be five calendar days late before any fee applies, counting the day after the due date as day one. Monthly rent allows fifteen dollars or five percent of the rent, whichever is greater, and weekly rent allows four dollars or five percent on the same terms. One fee per late payment is the limit.

  • A late fee cannot be subtracted from next month's rent in a way that puts that rent in default.
  • No late fee may be charged for water or sewer service provided under G.S. 62-110(g).
  • On subsidized rent, fees are figured on the tenant's share alone.

sections.h2: Which other grounds support a complaint?
sections.html:
G.S. 42-26 names three: staying past the end of the term, breaking a lease condition that terminates the estate, and deserting the home while owing rent. A different complaint needs a fresh read of the lease and the statute.

One limit surprises landlords who provide utilities. Unpaid water, sewer or electric charges may not be the basis for ending a lease, so collect that money through another route.

A breach claim is strongest when the lease states the condition and the consequence in plain words. Keep the lease, any written demand, the delivery dates and proof of delivery. The magistrate decides by a preponderance of the evidence under G.S. 42-30, so paper matters.

sections.h2: What follows once the notice period has run?
sections.html:
The landlord files a complaint, and under G.S. 42-28 the clerk issues a summons naming a court date no more than seven days out, weekends and legal holidays excluded.

The state court system says small claims dates fall within 30 days of filing, and that eviction cases are usually heard within 10 to 15 days. Our eviction process page follows the case from the complaint to the sheriff.

When the magistrate awards possession, the sheriff carries out the writ. The sheriff must warn the tenant of the approximate time, and the writ must be executed within five days of reaching the sheriff, under G.S. 42-36.2.

sections.h2: What can a tenant pay to cure a default after the case is filed?
sections.html:
A tenant who cures can end the case early, and the cure amount may include more than rent. Under G.S. 42-46, the landlord may fold court filing fees, the cost of serving process and out-of-pocket litigation expenses into the figure needed to cure a default.

Reasonable attorney fees can be added too, if a written lease provides for them, up to fifteen percent of the amount owed, or fifteen percent of the monthly rent when the default is something other than unpaid rent. A written lease may also allow a complaint-filing fee of fifteen dollars or five percent of monthly rent, whichever is greater, when the tenant cures and the landlord dismisses before judgment.

Only one administrative fee may be kept for a single complaint, and the landlord cannot deduct that fee from later rent or call its nonpayment a new default. If you are the owner and you plan to sell, a cure that ends in a dismissed case can leave the tenant in place, so tell the buyer in writing.

sections.h2: How long should a landlord plan before a sale closes?
sections.html:
Add the pieces together. The notice period comes first, the court date follows within days, and the sheriff's window comes last.

  • Notice period from the table above, or ten days after a rent demand.
  • A summons date no more than seven days after issuance.
  • A hearing that is usually held within 10 to 15 days of filing.
  • Ten days for a tenant to appeal the magistrate's decision, which can delay enforcement if a bond is posted.
  • Up to five days for the sheriff to execute the writ.

These steps overlap in places, but a buyer who needs the house vacant should be told that each one can add time.

sections.h2: How do these notices affect a landlord who wants to sell?
sections.html:
Each tenancy type runs on its own clock, so the closing date has to be built around it. A buyer who wants a vacant house needs the notice period, the hearing and any appeal to fit before closing.

  • For a monthly tenancy, seven days ends the tenancy on paper, and removal of anyone who stays goes through the court.
  • For a yearly tenancy, the notice has to arrive a month or more before the year ends.
  • For a manufactured home space, plan on 60 days or more before the rental period ends.

A foreclosure sale shifts the clock. Under G.S. 45-21.16A, a tenant whose rental agreement began or renewed on October 1, 2007 or later may end it on 10 to 90 days' notice after the sale date. That statute also says the notice of sale for a residential property with fewer than 15 rental units must warn that an order for possession may issue.

sections.h2: What should an owner record before serving a notice?
sections.html:
Write down the tenancy type, the rental period, the due date and the date of each payment, then match them to the table and to the ground you plan to use.

  • Which tenancy applies and its notice period.
  • Any lease terms that go beyond the statute.
  • The date and method of delivery for the notice or rent demand.
  • Whether any of the amount owed is water, sewer or electric arrears.
  • Whether a fee you plan to charge fits G.S. 42-46.

The clerk of superior court in your county can supply the current complaint form and filing steps. A landlord-tenant attorney can review the notice before it is served.

faqs.q: What notice ends a monthly rental in North Carolina?
faqs.a: Seven days. G.S. 42-14 also sets two days for a weekly tenancy and at least one month before year end for a yearly one.

faqs.q: How soon must a tenant pay once the landlord demands the rent?
faqs.a: Within ten days. G.S. 42-3 forfeits the lease term if the past-due rent stays unpaid after that, and the landlord may then re-enter.

faqs.q: Can unpaid electric or water charges end a lease?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 42-26 bars arrears for water, sewer or electric service from serving as the basis for termination.

faqs.q: What notice does a manufactured home lot renter get?
faqs.a: At least 60 days before the end of the rental period, under G.S. 42-14.

faqs.q: May a landlord lock the tenant out after serving notice?
faqs.a: No. Possession comes through a court judgment and a sheriff's writ. The clerk sets the court date within seven days of the summons under G.S. 42-28.
